card.title: When We Still Believed
card.instruction: Use a shared earlier hope as your emotional home base, returning to it whenever the present feels uncertain or disappointing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This napkin still says we'll open a bookshop by the sea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We drew that before rent became real.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We also drew two chairs by the window. Could we put ours together tonight?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: In the flat? I need to work at that window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After work, then. I'll bring our books. Ten minutes pretending we're in our seaside bookshop before we look at the bills.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 returns to the seaside-bookshop plan, A3 recreates its two chairs at home, and A5 protects a brief shared version before facing bills.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's rent reality causes A3's scaled-down chair proposal; B4's work-at-window need causes A5's after-work ten-minute arrangement.

relationship.evidence: B2 names financial reality and B4 has an actual work use for the window.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's work constraint to schedule a small emotional return without pretending the bills vanished.

specificity.evidence: A1 identifies the old napkin plan and B2 establishes the present financial pressure.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's books-before-bills interval makes the hope concrete and restrained rather than a generic optimistic line.
